lessons: Review snag only; checks were green. Remove `Journal.for_reading`: it builds the object with `cls.__new__` and skips `__init__`, so `append`, `close` and `with` raise AttributeError. It also adds a public API the Scope out does not allow.

Give segment parsing one owner: a module-level `_read_segments(directory)` that yields `tuple(_read_segment(path, active=path == segs[-1]))`. `Journal.read_segments()` returns it, `Journal.read()` flattens it, and `read_events` flattens it too.

`audit_journal` must not open a writer, because `Journal(...)` opens an append handle and can repair a torn tail. Read through a module-level `read_segments(state_dir)` next to `read_events` that shares `_read_segments`.

Update `tests/test_journal.py`: the torn-tail test must use `read_segments(state_dir)` or a `Journal` built with `with`, not `for_reading`. Keep the rolled-segment corruption test and the active-tail tolerance test.

Keep everything else, which the reviewer accepted: the audit invariants, the fixtures, the production-Runner green runs with one shared `Drive` (separate Drives restart the fake clock and trip `ts_monotone`), and CLI exit codes 0/1/2.
reason: One fixable scope and design snag with a concrete fix, and all mechanical checks passed, so rerun at the same capability.
